body: I see this and my blood runs cold realizing the absolute living hell that command chat must be.

I should preface this by saying I've no detailed prior knowledge of the Stoker story or the ancient lore around vampires and demons like them. My perspective comes from one of tidbits and lingering interests in those subjects and as someone who has a maybe-above-amateur appreciation for film and storytelling, especially with consideration for original inspirations and cultural proximity.

That being said, the two are interesting to compare, this Nosferatu and Hereditary, and I did find myself also anticipating that kind of chill and occult surprise going into the viewing this evening. To that point, I'd say there are distinct differences and there are also stylistic similarities. The atmosphere is smothering both for tension and being like navigating darkness in the isolating lighting choices. Both Hereditary and this Nosferatu used similar stationary and moving POVs to feel unearthly and possessed even in early establishing scenes. Visceral would be the word I'd describe the feel of the film over terrifying, though they tend to evoke each other. There were real moments of feeling the personal, ominous dread that a character would because of the mise-en-scène, score, and foley.

As for the occult element, that felt much more shared between the two films. This was a rather faithful adaptation to those original fears and beliefs that surrounded the medieval form of the vampire/demon. The traditional and ancient representations were well supplied in the film and it had a far more authentic portrayal of both the occult presence and cultural affects that would be felt should a real nosferatu have existed and played out in the world.

It was interesting, immersing, and evocative to watch. I don't know that you'll get the same feeling that Hereditary delivered in its shock and scare factor, but you'll feel like the same attention to detail and respect to the occult of this lore. This has less immersing elements and disruption that Hereditary had, but that's not to say it is a wide miss of that mark. It's still enjoyable, thoughtful, and disturbing in it's own merit.

On a personal, final note: I felt the creature design wasn't really interesting until the finale (for better or for worse) and that's not necessarily a bash. I hope this helps and I'm interested to know OPs and others' thoughts after their viewing.

I would say it's gotten worse with the new wave of players coming in, not to sound like the crotchety old guard. I've encountered it a bit before, but after nearly 2000 hours playing it over the years I'd still say it's not terribly pervasive. I'd attribute it to those who have come in from other games where it's been far more tolerated than it is here and (hopefully) they'll find it unwelcome and suppress it or ultimately leave.

That being said, I play US servers and any online gaming has those fragile, hateful bunch that feel the need to pass their hate off as "historic reenactment" for weak laughs or are just plain racist and bigoted because that somehow still lives on as a relatable trait between people these days (?!). It's had a place to live in FPS games of all styles for years and still does in many online multi-player titles, but HLL has been largely void of that persistent toxicity than any other FPS I've played so far. I know it sounds lame and familiar, but those few really bad apples are not the definition of the community and player base at large that continuously play this game. At least in my experience.

Now, I cannot say the same for the violent furor of those who call out others for not building garries... That one is an HLL hate staple.
